claim: Wild-type (WT) and Cd80/86−/− mice mount similar antigen-specific CD8+ T cell responses in magnitude during LCMV infection after both high and low viral inoculum dosages.
source: Effector CD8+ T cell formation during LCMV infection seems not to be driven by the main costimulatory CD28/B7 pathway because wild-type (WT) mice and mice deficient in both B7.1 and B7.2 (Cd80/86−/−) mount similar antigen-specific responses in magnitude, and this phenomenon is apparent after both high and low viral inoculum dosages (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A comparing WT and Cd80/86−/− mice infected with different doses of LCMV.

claim: During infection with VV or Listeria monocytogenes (LM), antigen-specific CD8+ T cell responses are highly reduced in the absence of B7-mediated costimulation.
source: In contrast, during infection with VV or Listeria monocytogenes (LM), antigen-specific CD8+ T cell responses are highly reduced in the absence of B7-mediated costimulation (Figure 1B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1B and 1C comparing responses in WT and Cd80/86−/− mice.

claim: CD8+ T cell responses against MCMV are dependent on B7-mediated costimulation, ranging from approximately sevenfold diminished responses for non-inflationary M45 and M57-specific responses to approximately 2.5-fold for inflationary m139 and M38-specific responses.
source: CD8+ T cell responses against MCMV are dependent on B7-mediated costimulation as well, ranging from ∼sevenfold diminished responses in case of the non-inflationary M45 and M57-specific to ∼2.5-fold in case of the inflationary m139 and M38-specific responses (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D comparing MCMV-specific responses in WT and Cd80/86−/− mice.

claim: Effector cell differentiation of virus-specific CD8+ T cells required B7-mediated costimulation in MCMV but not in LCMV infection.
source: Effector cell differentiation of virus-specific CD8+ T cells, indicated by the downregulation of CD62L and upregulation of CD44, also required B7-mediated costimulation in MCMV but not in LCMV infection (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1 analyzing CD44 and CD62L expression.

claim: CTLA-4 blockade during LCMV infection had no effect on T cell expansion.
source: Remarkably, CTLA-4 blockade during LCMV infection had no effect on T cell expansion, indicating that LCMV-specific CD8+ T cells are rather indifferent to enhanced B7-mediated signals (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2A and 2B comparing LCMV-specific responses with and without CTLA-4 blockade.

claim: CTLA-4 blockade during MCMV infection augmented MCMV-specific CD8+ T cell responses approximately threefold in a B7-dependent manner.
source: However, CTLA-4 blockade during MCMV infection augmented MCMV-specific CD8+ T cell responses ∼threefold in a B7-dependent manner (Figure 2C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2C and 2D comparing MCMV-specific responses with CTLA-4 blockade in WT and Cd80/86−/− mice.

claim: The GP33-specific CD8+ T cell response elicited by both MCMV-IE2-GP33 and MCMV-M45-GP33 was dependent on B7-mediated costimulation.
source: As determined by intracellular IFN-γ staining after restimulation (Figure 3A,B) or direct staining with MHC class I tetramers (data not shown), the GP33-specific CD8+ T cell response elicited by both MCMV-IE2-GP33 and MCMV-M45-GP33 was dependent on B7-mediated costimulation, albeit to a higher degree when the GP33 epitope was inserted within the M45 protein.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3A and 3B comparing GP33-specific responses in WT and Cd80/86−/− mice infected with recombinant MCMV.

claim: Infection with MCMV containing the model epitope OVA257-264 (SIINFEKL) inserted in the M45 protein resulted in an antigen-specific T cell response that depended on B7-mediated costimulation.
source: Infection with an MCMV containing the model epitope OVA257-264 (SIINFEKL) inserted in the M45 protein (MCMV-M45-SIINFEKL) resulted also in an antigen-specific T cell response that depended on B7-mediated costimulation (Figure 3C), indicating that non-viral epitopes elicit similar costimulation dependent responses.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C comparing SIINFEKL-specific responses in WT and Cd80/86−/− mice.

claim: LM expressing the LCMV GP33 epitope (LM-GP33) induced GP33-specific CD8+ T cell responses that were highly dependent on B7-mediated costimulation.
source: Furthermore, LM expressing the LCMV GP33 epitope (LM-GP33) induced GP33-specific CD8+ T cell responses that were highly dependent on B7-mediated costimulation (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D comparing GP33-specific responses in WT and Cd80/86−/− mice infected with LM-GP33.

claim: Upon vaccination with a synthetic long peptide (SLP) containing the GP33 epitope, Cd80/86−/− mice mounted a defective GP33-specific CD8+ T cell response in comparison with WT mice.
source: Also, upon vaccination with a synthetic long peptide (SLP) containing the GP33 epitope, Cd80/86−/− mice mounted a defective GP33-specific CD8+ T cell response in comparison with WT mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2 comparing GP33-specific responses after SLP vaccination.

claim: B7-mediated costimulation was dispensable for P14 cell expansion in LCMV infection.
source: Similar as observed for the endogenous LCMV-specific CD8+ T cell expansion, B7-mediated costimulation was dispensable for P14 cell expansion in LCMV infection.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data using TCR transgenic P14 cells in LCMV infection context.

claim: For the expansion of P14 cells in MCMV-IE2-GP33 and LM-GP33 infection, B7-mediated signals were highly required.
source: Importantly, for the expansion of P14 cells in MCMV-IE2-GP33 and LM-GP33 infection, B7-mediated signals were highly required (Figure 3E), which corroborates that the inflammatory environment is predominantly determining the costimulatory requirements.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E comparing P14 cell expansion in different infection contexts.

claim: The context of viral epitope expression, rather than the intrinsic nature of the epitope or the antigen-specific CD8+ T cell population, influences the dependence on B7-mediated signals for T cell expansion.
source: Together, these data indicate that the context of viral epitope expression, rather than the intrinsic nature of the epitope or the antigen-specific CD8+ T cell population, influences the dependence on B7-mediated signals for T cell expansion.
evidence: The claim is inferred from multiple experiments showing that the same epitope (GP33) requires B7-mediated costimulation in some infection contexts but not others.

claim: Memory GP33-specific CD8+ T cells primed in the context of an LCMV infection showed a dispensable role for B7-mediated signals for secondary T cell expansion in an LCMV environment, but a strong requirement for these signals in an MCMV context.
source: Comparing the GP33-specific CD8+ T cell responses upon antigenic re-challenge revealed a dispensable role for B7-mediated signals for secondary T cell expansion in an LCMV environment, but a strong requirement for these signals in an MCMV context even though these cells were primed in an LCMV environment (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A using adoptive transfer of memory cells into different infection contexts.

claim: When memory GP33-specific CD8+ T cells that depended on B7-mediated signals during priming in MCMV infection were transferred and re-challenged in an LCMV or an MCMV environment, the viral context during secondary expansion determined the requirement on costimulatory signals.
source: Importantly, when memory GP33-specific CD8+ T cells that depended on B7-mediated signals during priming in MCMV infection were transferred and re-challenged in an LCMV or an MCMV environment, the viral context during secondary expansion again determined the requirement on costimulatory signals (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B using adoptive transfer of memory cells primed in MCMV context.

claim: During secondary T cell responses the viral context is dominant and determines the CD28/B7 costimulation dependency of virus-specific CD8+ T cells independent of the priming context.
source: Together, these data indicate that during secondary T cell responses the viral context is dominant and determines the CD28/B7 costimulation dependency of virus-specific CD8+ T cells independent of the priming context.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the adoptive transfer experiments showing that the recall environment, not the priming environment, determines costimulation requirements.

claim: Serum levels of IFNα were particularly high in LCMV infected mice compared to the serum levels in MCMV infected mice.
source: In contrast, serum levels of IFNα were particularly high in LCMV infected mice compared to the serum levels in MCMV infected mice (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A measuring IFNα levels in serum.

claim: At 24 hr LCMV induced higher expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines (Rantes, IL-6, KC, Mip-1β and MCP-1) compared to MCMV, but after 48 hr the concentrations of these cytokines were comparable.
source: Consistent with this, at 24 hr LCMV also induced higher expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines, which have been described to be downstream of type I IFN signaling (i.e., Rantes, IL-6, KC, Mip-1β and MCP-1) (Teijaro et al., 2013). However, after 48 hr the concentrations of these cytokines were comparable (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B measuring cytokine concentrations at different time points, and cites previous work on type I IFN signaling.

claim: Blocking type I interferon receptor (IFNAR) during LCMV infection resulted in severely diminished LCMV-specific CD8+ T cell responses in WT mice.
source: Blocking antibodies for the type I IFN receptor (IFNAR) were administered during LCMV infection and resulted in severely diminished LCMV-specific CD8+ T cell responses in WT mice (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C comparing LCMV-specific responses with and without IFNAR blockade.

claim: IFNAR blocking antibodies administrated in Cd80/86−/− mice severely hampered LCMV-specific responses.
source: IFNAR blocking antibodies administrated in Cd80/86−/− mice also severely hampered LCMV-specific responses (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C comparing LCMV-specific responses in Cd80/86−/− mice with and without IFNAR blockade.

claim: The LCMV-specific CD8+ T cell responses in WT mice with abrogated IFNAR signaling were comparable to those in IFNAR blocked Cd80/86−/− mice.
source: Notably, the LCMV-specific CD8+ T cell responses in WT mice with abrogated IFNAR signaling were comparable to those in IFNAR blocked Cd80/86−/− mice.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data comparing LCMV-specific responses under different conditions of IFNAR and B7 blockade.

claim: No differences in IFNα levels were detected between WT and Cd80/86−/− mice during LCMV infection.
source: Furthermore, no differences in IFNα levels were detected between WT and Cd80/86−/− mice (Figure 5D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D measuring IFNα levels in different mouse strains.

claim: Ifnar1−/− P14 cells transferred to WT recipients were severely hampered in expansion compared to Ifnar1+/+ P14 cells during LCMV infection.
source: Ifnar1−/− P14 cells transferred to WT recipients were severely hampered in expansion compared to Ifnar1+/+ P14 cells (Figure 5E), which is consistent with previous reports (Kolumam et al., 2005; Aichele et al., 2006; Wiesel et al., 2012; Crouse et al., 2014; Xu et al., 2014) and confirms that type I IFNs drive directly LCMV-specific CD8+ T cell expansion.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5E and is consistent with multiple cited previous studies.

claim: Ifnar1+/+ P14 cells in Cd80/86−/− mice expanded vigorously and comparable to WT host mice during LCMV infection.
source: Ifnar1+/+ P14 cells in Cd80/86−/− mice expanded vigorously and comparable to WT host mice.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data comparing P14 cell expansion in different host genotypes.

claim: Ifnar1−/− P14 cells failed to expand in Cd80/86−/− mice and showed a slightly weaker expansion potential as Ifnar1−/− P14 cells in WT mice during LCMV infection.
source: Importantly, Ifnar1−/− P14 cells failed to expand in Cd80/86−/− mice as well and showed a slightly weaker expansion potential as Ifnar1−/− P14 cells in WT mice (Figure 5E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5E comparing Ifnar1−/− P14 cell expansion in different host genotypes.

claim: Type I IFN signaling in expanding CD8+ T cells is slightly redundant with B7-mediated costimulation signals during LCMV infection.
source: These data show that type I IFNs act directly on LCMV-specific CD8+ T cells, and that in the absence of this signal 3 cytokine the non-dependence of B7-mediated costimulation in driving LCMV-specific T cell expansion is to some extent altered, indicating that type I IFN signaling in expanding CD8+ T cells is slightly redundant with B7-mediated costimulation signals.
evidence: The claim is inferred from experimental data showing that the absence of both type I IFN signaling and B7-mediated costimulation has a greater effect than either alone.

claim: Adoptive transfer of Ifnar1+/+ and Ifnar1−/− P14 cells in WT mice infected with MCMV-IE2-GP33 resulted in profound expansion of the Ifnar1+/+ P14 cells but also of Ifnar1−/− P14 cells, although slightly diminished compared to Ifnar1+/+ P14 cells.
source: Adoptive transfer of Ifnar1+/+ and Ifnar1−/− P14 cells in WT mice that were subsequently infected with MCMV-IE2-GP33 resulted in profound expansion of the Ifnar1+/+ P14 cells but also of Ifnar1−/− P14 cells, although slightly diminished compared to Ifnar1+/+ P14 cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data comparing P14 cell expansion in MCMV infection context.

claim: Adoptive transfer of P14 cells in Cd80/86−/− mice infected with MCMV-IE2-GP33 resulted in hampered expansion of Ifnar1+/+ and even more so of Ifnar1−/− P14 cells.
source: Adoptive transfer of P14 cells in Cd80/86−/− mice resulted in hampered expansion of Ifnar1+/+ and even more so of Ifnar1−/− P14 cells, indicating that CD8+ T cells that develop during MCMV infection are to a small degree affected by type I IFN signaling (in a somewhat redundant manner with B7-mediated costimulation) but are most critically dependent on B7-mediated signals (Figure 5F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5F comparing P14 cell expansion in Cd80/86−/− mice infected with MCMV.

claim: Addition of recombinant type I IFN on day 1 and 2 during MCMV-IE2-GP33 infection caused no significant increase in the expansion of the P14 cells either transferred in WT or Cd80/86−/− mice.
source: Addition of recombinant type I IFN on day 1 and 2 during MCMV-IE2-GP33 infection in mice that received Ifnar1+/+ and Ifnar1−/− P14 cells, caused no significant increase in the expansion of the P14 cells either transferred in WT or Cd80/86−/− mice, indicating that additional type I IFN signaling has negligible impact on B7-mediated signals that drive T cell expansion in MCMV infection (Figure 5F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5F comparing P14 cell expansion with and without recombinant IFN administration.

claim: Administration of recombinant type I IFN during peptide vaccination improved GP33-specific CD8+ T cell expansion.
source: Administration of recombinant type I IFN during peptide vaccination, however, improved GP33-specific CD8+ T cell expansion, which indicated that IFNα is able to enhance T cell expansion in a low inflammatory context (Figure 5G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5G comparing GP33-specific responses with and without IFNα administration during vaccination.

claim: Serum of mice that were infected for 2 days with LCMV transferred to MCMV-infected WT and Cd80/86−/− mice resulted in no differences in the magnitude of the MCMV-specific CD8+ T cell response.
source: To examine if the dependence of T cell expansion on B7-mediated costimulatory signals could be changed by other soluble factors than type I IFN, serum of mice that were infected for 2 days with LCMV was transferred to MCMV-infected WT and Cd80/86−/− mice. However, no differences were found in the magnitude of the MCMV-specific CD8+ T cell response (Figure 5H), indicating that soluble factors in the LCMV environment do not enhance MCMV-specific CD8+ T cell expansion.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5H comparing MCMV-specific responses with and without LCMV serum transfer.

claim: During co-infection with MCMV and LCMV, MCMV-specific responses were still dependent on B7-mediated signals whereas LCMV-specific CD8+ T cells were not.
source: Remarkably, during this co-infection, MCMV-specific responses were still dependent on B7-mediated signals whereas LCMV-specific CD8+ T cells were not (Figure 5I).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5I comparing virus-specific responses during co-infection in WT and Cd80/86−/− mice.

claim: During an LCMV and MCMV infection a unique local environment is induced that principally determines the costimulatory requirements of the activated antigen-specific CD8+ T cells.
source: Together, these data show that during an LCMV and MCMV infection a unique local environment is induced that principally determines the costimulatory requirements of the activated antigen-specific CD8+ T cells, and that direct type I IFN signaling in CD8+ T cells is slightly redundant with B7-mediated costimulation.
evidence: The claim is inferred from multiple experiments showing that the viral context determines costimulation requirements even during co-infection.

claim: Expression of both B7.1 and B7.2 was upregulated on CD11c+ and CD11b+ cells early in LCMV infection.
source: Expression of both B7.1 and B7.2 was upregulated on CD11c+ and CD11b+ cells early in infection (Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A measuring B7.1 and B7.2 expression on myeloid cells.

claim: Expression levels of B7.1 and B7.2 on CD11c+ and CD11b+ myeloid subsets were higher in LCMV infection as compared to MCMV infection.
source: Strikingly, expression levels of B7.1 and B7.2 on these myeloid subsets were higher in LCMV infection as compared to MCMV infection.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data comparing costimulatory ligand expression between LCMV and MCMV infections.

claim: Expression of both CD70 and 4-1BBL were much higher induced on CD11b+ and CD11c+ cells in LCMV infection as compared to MCMV infection.
source: Expression of both CD70 and 4-1BBL were much higher induced on CD11b+ and CD11c+ cells in LCMV infection as compared to MCMV infection (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 6A and 6B comparing costimulatory ligand expression.

claim: OX40L levels were increased in LCMV infection compared to MCMV infection, although this expression was relatively low.
source: Furthermore, OX40L levels were increased in LCMV infection as well, although this expression was relatively low (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 6A and 6B measuring OX40L expression.

claim: Compared to VV infection, elevated expression levels of all costimulatory ligands were observed on CD11b+ cells in the spleen in LCMV infection.
source: Also compared to VV infection, elevated expression levels of all costimulatory ligands were observed on CD11b+ cells in the spleen in LCMV infection (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A comparing costimulatory ligand expression between LCMV and VV infections.

claim: On CD11c+ cells, B7.2 and 4-1BBL expression was increased in LCMV infection but the levels of B7.1, CD70 and OX40L were comparable between VV and LCMV infection.
source: On CD11c+ cells, B7.2 and 4-1BBL expression was increased in LCMV infection but the levels of B7.1, CD70 and OX40L were comparable between VV and LCMV infection (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1 comparing costimulatory ligand expression on CD11c+ cells.

claim: The elevated costimulatory ligand expression levels found upon LCMV infection were partially associated with the high type I IFN levels within the LCMV-induced environment.
source: The elevated costimulatory ligand expression levels found upon LCMV infection were partially associated with the high type I IFN levels within the LCMV-induced environment, as abrogation of type I IFN signaling, resulted to some extent in diminished costimulatory ligand expression (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B comparing costimulatory ligand expression with and without IFNAR blockade.

claim: In Cd70−/− mice, no significant differences were found in the magnitude of the LCMV-specific CD8+ T cell response.
source: In Cd70−/− mice, no significant differences were found in the magnitude of the LCMV-specific CD8+ T cell response, indicating that the CD27/CD70 costimulatory pathway by itself has a limited or redundant role during LCMV infection (Figure 7A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A comparing LCMV-specific responses in WT and Cd70−/− mice.

claim: Both GP33- and NP396-specific responses were significantly diminished in Cd70/80/86−/− mice.
source: Both GP33- and NP396-specific responses were significantly diminished in Cd70/80/86−/− mice, indicating that CD70 and B7 molecules are redundantly required for LCMV-specific CD8+ T cell expansion, and that these molecules can compensate each other (Figure 7A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A comparing LCMV-specific responses in mice lacking both CD70 and B7 molecules.

claim: No significant differences were found when OX40L and 4-1BBL were blocked during LCMV infection, however, when both pathways were abrogated the magnitude of the LCMV-specific CD8+ T cell response was significantly diminished.
source: No significant differences were found when OX40L and 4-1BBL were blocked, however, when both pathways were abrogated the magnitude of the LCMV-specific CD8+ T cell response was significantly diminished (Figure 7A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 7A and 7B comparing LCMV-specific responses with different combinations of costimulatory pathway blockade.

claim: LCMV-specific CD8+ T cell responses were drastically decreased when OX40L/4-1BBL blockade was performed in mice lacking CD70 and B7-mediated costimulation.
source: Strikingly, LCMV-specific CD8+ T cell responses were drastically decreased when OX40L/4-1BBL blockade was performed in mice lacking CD70 and B7-mediated costimulation.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data comparing LCMV-specific responses under multiple costimulatory pathway blockades.

claim: IFNα levels in the serum of Cd70/80/86−/− mice were not substantially altered compared to WT mice during LCMV infection.
source: This diminished response was not due to defective induction of type I IFN, as IFNα levels in the serum of these mice were not substantially altered compared to WT mice (Figure 7C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7C measuring IFNα levels in different mouse strains.

claim: Virus-specific CD8+ T cell responses during LCMV infection critically depend on a plethora of costimulatory signals that are individually dispensable because they function in a highly redundant manner.
source: Together, these data indicate that virus-specific CD8+ T cell responses during LCMV infection critically depend on a plethora of costimulatory signals that are individually dispensable because they function in a highly redundant manner.
evidence: The claim is inferred from multiple experiments showing that blocking individual costimulatory pathways has minimal effect, but blocking multiple pathways severely impairs responses.

claim: MCMV-specific CD8+ T cell responses in Cd70−/− and Cd80/86−/− mice were significantly diminished, however responses in Cd70/80/86−/− mice were even lower.
source: MCMV-specific CD8+ T cell responses in Cd70−/− and Cd80/86−/− mice were significantly diminished, however responses in Cd70/80/86−/− mice were even lower (Figure 7E), indicating both a non-redundant and cooperative role for CD70 and B7-mediated costimulation in driving MCMV-specific T cell expansion.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7E comparing MCMV-specific responses in different costimulation-deficient mice.

claim: Upon dual blockade of OX40L and 4-1BBL-mediated interactions MCMV-specific T cell responses were not affected.
source: Moreover, we found that upon dual blockade of OX40L and 4-1BBL-mediated interactions MCMV-specific T cell responses were not affected as well (Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2 comparing MCMV-specific responses with OX40L/4-1BBL blockade.

claim: Redundancy between different costimulatory molecules is induced by the viral context.
source: These results indicate that redundancy between different costimulatory molecules is induced by the viral context.
evidence: The claim is inferred from comparing the redundancy patterns observed in LCMV versus MCMV infections.

claim: Ifnar1+/+ P14 cells expanded well in WT, Cd70−/− and Cd80/86−/− mice and were to some extend hampered in expansion in Cd70/80/86−/− mice during LCMV infection.
source: Similar to what is found for endogenous LCMV-specific CD8+ T cell responses, Ifnar1+/+ P14 cells expanded well in WT, Cd70−/− and Cd80/86−/− mice and were to some extend hampered in expansion in Cd70/80/86−/− mice (Figure 8A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8A comparing P14 cell expansion in different host genotypes.

claim: Ifnar1−/− P14 cells were rigorously hindered in their expansion when transferred in WT mice and even more so in costimulation deficient mice during LCMV infection.
source: The Ifnar1−/− P14 cells were rigorously hindered in their expansion, when transferred in WT mice and even more so in costimulation deficient mice.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data comparing Ifnar1−/− P14 cell expansion in different host genotypes.

claim: The reduced expansion of the Ifnar1−/− P14 cells in the costimulation deficient mice as compared to WT mice indicates slight redundancy of type I IFN signaling with costimulatory-driven signals in expanding CD8+ T cells.
source: This reduced expansion of the Ifnar1−/− P14 cells in the costimulation deficient mice as compared to WT mice indicates slight redundancy of type I IFN signaling with costimulatory-driven signals in expanding CD8+ T cells.
evidence: The claim is inferred from experimental data showing that the absence of both type I IFN signaling and costimulation has a greater effect than either alone.

claim: Ifnar1+/+ P14 cell expansion during MCMV-IE2-GP33 infection was critically dependent on both CD70- and B7-mediated costimulation.
source: Furthermore, Ifnar1+/+ P14 cells were transferred to mice that were infected with MCMV-IE2-GP33. In this setting, P14 cell expansion was critically dependent on both CD70- and B7-mediated costimulation (Figure 8B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8B comparing P14 cell expansion in different host genotypes infected with MCMV.

claim: Compared to Ifnar1 proficient P14 cells, Ifnar1 deficient P14 cells had a higher degree of type I IFN dependence in the absence of costimulation during MCMV infection, which was most pronounced when both CD70 and B7 costimulatory molecules were lacking.
source: Compared to Ifnar1 proficient P14 cells, Ifnar1 deficient P14 cells had a higher degree of type I IFN dependence in the absence of costimulation, which was most pronounced when both CD70 and B7 costimulatory molecules were lacking (Figure 8B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8B comparing Ifnar1+/+ and Ifnar1−/− P14 cell expansion in different host genotypes.

claim: Type I IFNs have a slight stimulating activity for CD8+ T cells in MCMV infection, which is more pronounced in the absence of CD70 and B7-mediated signaling.
source: Thus, type I IFNs have a slight stimulating activity for CD8+ T cells in MCMV infection, which is more pronounced in the absence of CD70 and B7-mediated signaling, indicating that also during MCMV infection partial redundancy of type I IFN signaling with costimulation during CD8+ T cell expansion occurs.
evidence: The claim is inferred from experimental data showing differential effects of type I IFN signaling in the presence or absence of costimulation.

claim: The pathogen-induced environment dictates the utilization of costimulatory signals that drive CD8+ T cell expansion.
source: Using different viral models we show that the pathogen-induced environment dictates the utilization of costimulatory signals that drive CD8+ T cell expansion.
evidence: The claim is inferred from multiple experiments showing that different pathogens induce different costimulation requirements.

claim: Primary LCMV-specific CD8+ T cell responses have long been considered to be costimulation independent.
source: Primary LCMV-specific CD8+ T cell responses have long been considered to be costimulation independent (Shahinian et al., 1993; Kundig et al., 1996; Andreasen et al., 2000; Grujic et al., 2010; Eberlein et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to multiple previous studies.

claim: The development of LCMV-specific memory CD8+ T cell formation is hampered during Cd28 or Cd80/86 deficiency.
source: Nevertheless, the development of LCMV-specific memory CD8+ T cell formation is hampered during Cd28 or Cd80/86 deficiency (Grujic et al., 2010; Eberlein et al., 2012), indicating that CD28/B7-mediated costimulation occurs during LCMV infection, which is in agreement with our study.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies and is consistent with the current study's findings.

claim: The CD27/CD70 pathway has negligible costimulatory effects for LCMV-specific CD8+ T cell expansion when solely this pathway is abrogated.
source: We also found that the CD27/CD70 pathway has negligible costimulatory effects for LCMV-specific CD8+ T cell expansion when solely this pathway is abrogated. This has been observed by others as well (Matter et al., 2005; Schildknecht et al., 2007), but recent reports suggested that blockade of the CD27/CD70 pathway can to some extend impair CD8+ T cell responses during acute LCMV infection (Penaloza-Macmaster et al., 2011; Munitic et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by the current study's data and is consistent with some cited previous studies, while acknowledging conflicting reports.

claim: Unhampered LCMV-specific responses are observed upon dual 4-1BBL and CD28 abrogation.
source: Unhampered LCMV-specific responses are observed upon dual 4-1BBL and CD28 abrogation (DeBenedette et al., 1999) and this is consistent with our data showing that multiple pathways than these have to be abrogated to observe diminished LCMV-specific CD8+ T cell responses virus-specific responses.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study and is consistent with the current study's findings.

claim: Strong replicating VV-strains employ more costimulatory receptors as compared to weak replicating VV-strains.
source: Strong replicating VV-strains employ more costimulatory receptors as compared to weak replicating VV-strains (Salek-Ardakani et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: 4-1BBL-mediated interactions are critical during severe influenza virus infections but dispensable upon a mild influenza virus.
source: Furthermore, 4-1BBL-mediated interactions are critical during severe influenza virus infections but dispensable upon a mild influenza virus (Lin et al., 2009), indicating that the strength of the inflammatory environment dictates the employment of different costimulatory receptors.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study and is used to support the interpretation of the current findings.

claim: During MCMV infection, the B7.1 and B7.2 expression in virus-infected cells is downmodulated by the virus by sophisticated immune evasion mechanism.
source: During MCMV infection for example, the B7.1 and B7.2 expression in virus-infected cells is downmodulated by the virus by sophisticated immune evasion mechanism (Loewendorf et al., 2004; Mintern et al., 2006; Arens et al., 2011a).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The CD8+ T cell response to MCMV is predominantly mediated by cross-priming APCs, which are by definition not directly infected by the virus.
source: Perhaps related to this, is that the CD8+ T cell response to MCMV is predominantly mediated by cross-priming APCs, which are by definition not directly infected by the virus (Torti et al., 2011; Busche et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: TNFR family members are known to signal via TRAF molecules, which are coupled to the activation of the NF-κB pathway via both the canonical and the non-canonical routes.
source: TNFR family members are known to signal via TRAF molecules, which are coupled to the activation of the NF-κB pathway via both the canonical and the non-canonical routes (Croft, 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study and represents established scientific knowledge.

claim: CD28 is able to signal via the NF-κB route.
source: CD28 is also able to signal via the NF-κB route (Boomer and Green, 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Redundancy between CD28 and CD27 signaling on CD8+ T cell expansion has been found in influenza virus infection.
source: We found redundancy between CD28 and CD27 signaling on CD8+ T cell expansion in MCMV and LCMV infection, and this has been found in influenza virus infection as well (Hendriks et al., 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by the current study's data and citation to a previous study.

claim: In influenza virus infection, virus-specific T cells that accumulate in the lung but not in the spleen were collectively dependent on signals mediated via a variety of TNFR family members.
source: The latter is consistent with observations in the influenza virus infection model, where virus-specific T cells that accumulate in the lung but not in the spleen were collectively dependent on signals mediated via a variety of TNFR family members (Hendriks et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study and is used to support the interpretation of the current findings.

claim: The majority of the MCMV-specific CD8+ T cells is activated via cross-priming.
source: The majority of the MCMV-specific CD8+ T cells is activated via cross-priming (Torti et al., 2011; Busche et al., 2013), and whether both direct and cross-priming occur during LCMV infection is unclear (Freigang et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: CD11c+ APCs are critical for LCMV-specific CD8+ T cell priming.
source: Nevertheless CD11c+ APCs are critical for LCMV-specific CD8+ T cell priming (Probst and van den Broek, 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Because of different tropisms it is unlikely that MCMV and LCMV co-infect the very same cells and that the viral epitopes are presented by the same APC.
source: Moreover, because of different tropisms it is unlikely that MCMV and LCMV co-infect the very same cells and that the viral epitopes are presented by the same APC (Matloubian et al., 1993; Alexandre et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is inferred from established knowledge about viral tropisms and is supported by citations.

claim: APCs need to be directly activated for adequate T cell priming rather than by environmental inflammatory signals.
source: Since APCs need to be directly activated for adequate T cell priming rather than by environmental inflammatory signals (Kratky, 2011), our data are consistent with a scenario where the two viruses activate APCs in a different manner resulting in differential provision of costimulatory signals.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study and is used to interpret the current findings.

claim: LCMV and MCMV are both natural mouse pathogens and infection with these viruses results in virus levels that peak around day 4 post-infection in the spleen and liver.
source: However, LCMV and MCMV are both natural mouse pathogens and infection with these viruses results in virus levels that peak around day 4 post-infection in the spleen and liver (Buchmeier et al., 1980; Cicin-Sain et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The pathogen-specific inflammatory environment dictates the fate of responding CD8+ T cells allowing shaping of effector and memory T cell formation.
source: Perhaps related to our results are the observations that the pathogen-specific inflammatory environment dictates the fate of responding CD8+ T cells allowing shaping of effector and memory T cell formation (Obar et al., 2011; Keppler et al., 2012; Plumlee et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies and is used to contextualize the current findings.

claim: The requirements for CD28/B7-mediated costimulation can differ for primary and memory cells in vitro.
source: Although in vitro the requirements for CD28/B7-mediated costimulation can differ for primary and memory cells (Flynn and Mullbacher, 1996), we found in vivo that CD28/B7-mediated costimulation was important for the expansion of both naive and memory CD8+ T cells in MCMV infection.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study and contrasts with the current study's in vivo findings.

claim: Models of influenza virus, VV and murine γ-herpesvirus require B7-mediated signals for primary and secondary expansion of virus-specific CD8+ T cells.
source: This is consistent with models of influenza virus, VV and murine γ-herpesvirus (Borowski et al., 2007; Fuse et al., 2008) that require B7-mediated signals for primary and secondary expansion of virus-specific CD8+ T cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies and is consistent with the current findings.

claim: Type I IFNs are not required for the expansion of human memory CD8+ T cells in vitro.
source: Type I IFNs are not required for the expansion of human memory CD8+ T cells in vitro (Hervas-Stubbs et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: In experimental in vivo models, the inflammatory environment determines the signal 3 (i.e., type I IFN and IL-12 signaling) dependency upon secondary infection independent of the context of priming.
source: In experimental in vivo models, however, the inflammatory environment determines the signal 3 (i.e., type I IFN and IL-12 signaling) dependency upon secondary infection independent of the context of priming (Keppler and Aichele, 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study and is consistent with the current findings.

claim: The viral context determined the dependence on CD28/B7-mediated costimulation for expansion of naive and memory CD8+ T cells.
source: We examined the underlying mechanisms of this differential T cell costimulation dependence and found that the viral context determined the dependence on CD28/B7-mediated costimulation for expansion of naive and memory CD8+ T cells, indicating that the requirement for costimulatory signals is not imprinted.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from adoptive transfer experiments showing that the recall environment determines costimulation requirements.

claim: Related to the high-level costimulatory molecule expression induced by LCMV, CD28/B7-mediated costimulation was dispensable for accumulation of LCMV-specific CD8+ T cells because of redundancy with the costimulatory pathways induced by TNF receptor family members (i.e., CD27, OX40, and 4-1BB).
source: Notably, related to the high-level costimulatory molecule expression induced by lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV), CD28/B7-mediated costimulation was dispensable for accumulation of LCMV-specific CD8+ T cells because of redundancy with the costimulatory pathways induced by TNF receptor family members (i.e., CD27, OX40, and 4-1BB).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing that multiple costimulatory pathways must be blocked to impair LCMV-specific responses.

claim: Type I IFN signaling in viral-specific CD8+ T cells is slightly redundant with costimulatory signals.
source: Type I IFN signaling in viral-specific CD8+ T cells is slightly redundant with costimulatory signals.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing that the absence of both type I IFN signaling and costimulation has a greater effect than either alone.

claim: Pathogen-specific conditions differentially and uniquely dictate the utilization of costimulatory pathways allowing shaping of effector and memory antigen-specific CD8+ T cell responses.
source: These results highlight that pathogen-specific conditions differentially and uniquely dictate the utilization of costimulatory pathways allowing shaping of effector and memory antigen-specific CD8+ T cell responses.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion inferred from all the experimental data presented in the study.
